title: India pledges ₹15,000 crore to Nepal, mostly as credit, as Shah visit ends with eight pacts
dek: A ₹3,500 crore grant and an ₹11,500 crore credit line for energy, eight MoUs and a call to start the Siliguri–Jhapa oil pipeline. Boundary issues were left to the foreign secretaries.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
India will give Nepal a development package of ₹15,000 crore (24,000 crore Nepalese rupees) to rebuild after this year's floods and to finance energy projects, the two governments said on Monday at the end of Prime Minister Balendra Shah's State visit to New Delhi. The package was announced after Mr Shah's talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi at Hyderabad House, alongside eight memorandums of understanding and a joint vision for the relationship.

The 24-point joint press release splits the package into a ₹3,500 crore grant for post-disaster reconstruction and new infrastructure, and an ₹11,500 crore rupee-denominated line of credit for energy projects. The individual projects and the terms will be settled through "mutual consultations", it said. The two leaders also laid foundation stones for a 669 MW hydropower project and a petroleum terminal in Jhapa, the Nepali district on the border with north Bengal, and called for work on a Siliguri–Jhapa oil pipeline to start "at the earliest".

## What happened

Mr Shah's visit on 22 and 23 November was his first to India since he became prime minister in March. According to the joint release, the talks covered bilateral cooperation, regional issues and global developments. Mr Shah "acknowledged with appreciation India's humanitarian and technical support" after the Rasuwa-Bhotekoshi floods, which the release said caused "significant loss of life and destruction of property".

The leaders adopted a Joint Vision for "Viksit Bharat and Samunnat Nepal" (a developed India and a prosperous Nepal). It covers trade, connectivity, energy, water, climate resilience, digital services, space and sport, and reports said it rests on 10 pillars.

The eight MoUs cover:

- forensic science and police research (National Forensic Sciences University and Nepal Police)
- police training (Rashtriya Raksha University and Nepal Police Academy)
- civil-service training (National Centre for Good Governance and Nepal Administrative Staff College)
- Ayurveda and traditional medicine
- satellite communication over the South Asia Satellite (ISRO and Nepal's Ministry of Information and Communication)
- sustainable urban development
- health and medicine
- livestock and fisheries

India will also set up an offshore campus of an Indian Institute of Technology in Nepal, and the two sides agreed to make banking and telephone services easier to use for each other's citizens.

## Connectivity and energy

Nepal gets a new transit route for its trade through Deendayal Port at Kandla in Gujarat, with access to Paradip in Odisha to follow once the infrastructure is ready. The leaders flagged off the Sarayu-Kamala Express between Ayodhya and Janakpur. The location survey for a broad-gauge line from Raxaul to Kathmandu has been finalised, and India will help with Nepal's East-West Railway. A road bridge between Dharchula in India and Darchula in Nepal was opened, and a foundation stone was laid for an integrated check post at Banbasa.

On air links, the one-way B345 route (Kathmandu–Bhairahawa–Lucknow) is to become two-way after technical consultations. Other aviation proposals "currently under discussion" will be taken up later, the release said. It did not mention the new entry routes Nepal had sought or the reported dispute over a route near Bagdogra, the airport serving Siliguri.

In energy, the leaders dedicated Phase II of the Motihari–Amlekhgunj petroleum pipeline, laid a virtual foundation stone for the 669 MW Lower Arun hydroelectric project, and directed work on the detailed project report for the Pancheshwar project and faster work on reports for Saptakoshi and Sunkoshi. They welcomed progress towards joint ventures for two cross-border transmission lines, Inaruwa–New Purnea and Dodhara–Bareilly, and agreed to explore gas pipelines.

## What they said

> "We are partners in each other's progress." – Prime Minister Narendra Modi

Mr Modi said the package would "help affected families get their lives back on track", according to reports, and that India had kept up supplies of petroleum products, fertiliser and other essentials to Nepal despite this year's oil-supply problems. Mr Shah called India a "dependable neighbour" and a "consistent first responder" in disasters, reports said. "The relations between India and Nepal stand as firm as the Himalayas," he said, and added: "I warmly welcome Indian investors to Nepal." Mr Shah invited Mr Modi to visit Nepal; Mr Modi accepted, with dates to be fixed through diplomatic channels.

## Background

The floods began on 26 August, when a glacier collapse near Nepal's border with China sent mud and rock into the Trishuli river. About 1,500 people were killed and another 5,200 are missing, presumed dead, according to reports. Roads, bridges and power lines were washed away.

Before the visit Nepal had asked for about $2 billion, made up of $1 billion in soft loans, $500 million in grants and $500 million for rebuilding, according to reports. The package announced on Monday is worth about $1.62 billion, one report said, and most of it is credit rather than grant. Indian reports differ slightly on the rupee figure: some give ₹15,103 crore, while the joint release says ₹15,000 crore.

Two sensitive issues got only brief mention. Nepal claims Kalapani, Lipulekh and Limpiyadhura, which India administers, and protested in May when India and China agreed to reopen border trade through the Lipulekh pass. The joint release does not name the areas: it says the leaders noted progress on repairing boundary pillars and "directed the Foreign Secretaries to work on outstanding boundary issues".

## Why it matters for India and Bengal

Nepal borders five Indian states, including West Bengal, and India and China compete for influence in Kathmandu. While Mr Shah was in Delhi, a Nepali parliamentary team was in China to discuss stalled infrastructure projects and closed border trading points, according to reports. The energy credit line and the hydropower and transmission projects bind Nepal's power sector more closely to the Indian grid. Nepal already exports about 1,200 MW of electricity to India, reports said.

For north Bengal, the Siliguri–Jhapa pipeline and the Jhapa terminal would carry Indian fuel across the border near Siliguri, through a corridor already central to trade with Nepal and Bhutan. The release gave no timeline for the pipeline.

## What happens next

The two sides will now work out which projects the grant and the credit line will pay for. The Sarayu-Kamala Express is due to start regular weekly runs on 28 November, according to reports. Technical talks on the B345 air route and other aviation proposals are still to be scheduled, as is Mr Modi's visit to Nepal.
